id_right_flank_the.blurb: Bear Creek Wall, on the Lost River Range's southwest side near Leslie, splits into four parts; the Right Flank is one of them. It holds 18 climbs, mostly gear-protected with a handful of bolted lines, all in the 5.10 to 5.12 range and weighted toward 5.11 and 5.12. The limestone here is laid back rather than vertical, rewarding good footwork, and the protection leans on natural features, so expect an adventurous feel more than a polished sport crag. Routes run from short single pitches to a two-pitch line of roughly 250 feet. It is a remote, uncrowded spot reached by a rough canyon road and a long walk.

id_drilling_fields_lost_world.blurb: At City of Rocks in south-central Idaho, Lost World is a little friction slab tucked into a recess along the eastern edge of the Drilling Fields. All 18 climbs are bolted, and the grades cluster around 5.10 with a few gentler routes at the bottom end and a couple of 5.11s and a single 5.12 at the top. The surface is gritty slab with bands of moss near the tops of the lines, so it suits climbers who enjoy delicate footwork. It sees little traffic compared with the better-known City of Rocks walls, and a later-in-the-day visit helps with both sun and company.

id_picnic_crag.blurb: Picnic Crag is the northernmost of three basalt crags along one cliff band in the Snake River Canyon at Shoshone Falls, just outside Twin Falls. It has 18 sport routes with a broad spread: a few easy leads, a solid block of 5.9 to 5.11, and a couple of harder lines up to 5.13. The rock is featured basalt facing west, so it gets afternoon sun, and the canyon views are a bonus. Together with its neighbor The Midway it is a popular choice for newer climbers, groups and families, and the short walk from the car keeps logistics simple.
id_picnic_crag.parking_note: Drive into the Snake River Canyon toward Shoshone Falls and keep left at the fork. Leave the car by the Welcome to Shoshone Falls sign just past a tight horseshoe bend, or alternatively at the boat ramp above the falls.
id_picnic_crag.approach: From the parking area by the sign, follow the trail north past The Midway; the crag is a minute or two further along the same cliff band. From the boat ramp, a short trail climbs to the base.

id_all_american_wall.blurb: All American Wall is the left-most wall of the All American Area at Massacre Rocks, across the Snake River from American Falls in eastern Idaho. It holds 17 climbs, almost all of them bolted sport routes plus a single gear line, spanning 5.9 to 5.12 with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. It is a good pick for intermediate climbers looking for steady mileage on steep, bolted walls. It is the first wall you meet when walking in from the west rim, so it is easy to combine with neighboring walls.

id_gang_fight_wall.blurb: Gang Fight Wall sits in a sheltered alcove at the end of the west rim at Massacre Rocks, near American Falls in eastern Idaho. Its 17 routes are all bolted sport lines on basalt, ranging from 5.9 to 5.13 with the strongest concentration at 5.11 and 5.12, so it is mostly for climbers already comfortable on steep, sustained ground. The south-facing alcove catches the sun and blocks wind, which makes it a pleasant option on cold days, while summer afternoons will be hot. The walk from where the road ends is very short.
